questions.question: What happens if the true language is excluded from langid.py's active candidate set?
options: The classifier returns an automatic unknown label
The classifier chooses among the remaining candidates and may be confidently wrong
The model adds the missing language dynamically
Normalization restores the excluded label
questions.explanation: Classification is constrained to the active labels. A normalized score cannot make an excluded truth eligible.

questions.question: Why can the same text receive a different normalized score after candidate restriction?
options: The text is automatically translated
The score summarizes competition within the active candidate set
The package retrains the model on every request
The byte length changes when candidates change
questions.explanation: Candidate restriction changes which labels compete, so the normalized distribution can change even though the input is identical.

questions.question: Which policy best protects a language-specific downstream route?
options: Always accept the highest label
Use one universal score threshold copied from a tutorial
Calibrate on labeled slices and gate score, evidence, scope, mixed input, and fallback behavior
Discard the normalized score and route randomly
questions.explanation: The application must combine model evidence with the actual decision cost and an explicit abstention path.

questions.question: Why build a dedicated LanguageIdentifier for a stable candidate policy in a concurrent service?
options: It prevents request-level mutation of the module's shared language set
It changes ISO codes into full language names
It guarantees calibrated probabilities
It removes the bundled model from memory
questions.explanation: A dedicated classifier keeps candidate-set state inside a stable worker or route boundary instead of racing on module-level mutation.

questions.question: What is the correct response to short or mixed-language input outside the evaluated envelope?
options: Force the top document-level label into production
Treat a high score as proof that every span has one language
Defer to a declared fallback or classify a better-defined unit
Add more decimal places to the score
questions.explanation: Abstention preserves the contract when the input unit does not match what the routing decision was evaluated to handle.

questions.question: Which model design does the original langid.py paper describe?
options: A transformer over sentence embeddings
A multinomial Naive Bayes classifier over selected byte n-grams
A rule-only dictionary lookup
A speech-recognition decoder
questions.explanation: The original system uses selected byte n-gram features, a compiled scanner, and multinomial Naive Bayes scoring.
